name: Dolores River
agency: BLM Tres Rios Field Office / San Juan National Forest

camps.name: Bradfield Recreation Site
camps.desc: A campground a quarter mile below the bridge, with toilets, potable water, a ramp and parking. $8 a night.

camps.name: Box Elder
camps.desc: Limited primitive camping just below Mountain Sheep Point Recreation Site. No fee.

camps.name: Roadside camps
camps.desc: An unimproved dirt road runs along river left for the first half of this reach, with roadside campsites.

camps.name: River-right camps
camps.desc: A couple of good campsites on river right.

rapids.name: Ponderosa Gorge
rapids.desc: The first ten miles run Class II through ponderosa pine and Douglas fir on the benches above the river.

rapids.name: Snaggletooth
rapids.desc: The biggest rapid on the upper river, with the line changing with flow, and it has been portaged as often as run. Easy to run into before you realize it: approach carefully and scout from river left. A dirt road on river left offers a portage.

rapids.name: Island
rapids.desc: Long and continuous. Below about 800 cfs exposed rocks create hazards for rafts.

rapids.name: The Wall (Cannonball)
rapids.desc: A bedrock wall at the bottom right requires a hard left pull.

rapids.name: Bull Canyon
rapids.desc: An outwash rapid entering from river right; much bigger than usual at high flows.

rapids.name: Sleeping Rock
rapids.desc: Emerges at flows under 1,000 cfs; easier at higher flows.

rapids.name: Spring Canyon
rapids.desc: An outwash rapid. A hike to a pool and grotto about a mile up the canyon.

rapids.name: One Holer
rapids.desc: Stay left of the island to reach the hole at the bottom.

rapids.name: La Sal
rapids.desc: Above La Sal Canyon. Scout it, especially at lower flows.

hikes.name: Spring Canyon
hikes.desc: A hike to a pool and grotto about a mile up the canyon.

hikes.name: La Sal Canyon
hikes.desc: A side canyon hike below La Sal Rapid.

rules.d: The river runs only when McPhee Dam releases. The season is usually April to early June, depending on snowpack, and can be short or absent. Check the Dolores Water Conservancy District for the release schedule.
About 200 cfs for canoes, kayaks and duckies; 800 cfs for rafts under 14 feet; 1,000 cfs for larger rafts.
Flows generally peak late April to early May. Releases of about 3,400 cfs have been reported in May.
Scout Snaggletooth and The Wall, and La Sal Rapid at lower flows. Snaggletooth is easy to run into before you realize it.
Willows have encroached on the channel in low-flow years, making it harder to eddy out and reach camp.
Once in Slick Rock Canyon, exit options are limited.
The Dolores and its tributaries are not fit to drink. Bring your drinking water.
Much of the first 15 miles below Slickrock crosses private ranch land. Respect landowners; the BLM manages the river corridor.
Campsites in Slick Rock Canyon are infrequent because of surrounding private land, and popular ones fill quickly.

landmarks.name: Bradfield Bridge
landmarks.desc: Put-in. Bradfield Recreation Site is on river left a quarter mile below the bridge, about 6 miles east of Cahone. Sign in at the put-in. Likely the 1776 camp of the Dominguez-Escalante expedition.

landmarks.name: Mountain Sheep Point
landmarks.desc: Recreation site with a ramp, toilets and limited parking, also called Dove Creek Pump Station. Reached by County Road J from Highway 666. A common stopping point and take-out for a one-day trip of 19 miles.

landmarks.name: Slickrock
landmarks.desc: The Highway 141 bridge. The access is on private land, with a landowner fee of $10 per day for parking and launching. Once in Slick Rock Canyon, exits are limited.

landmarks.name: Gypsum Valley
landmarks.desc: BLM boat ramp on river right, reached by Highway 20 off Highway 141. Skips about 14 miles through private ranchland.

landmarks.name: Bedrock
landmarks.desc: Take-out on river left just upstream of the Highway 90 bridge. Beyond it the river continues 10 miles to the San Miguel confluence and on to Gateway.

access.name: Grand Junction
access.note: Nearest large city to the take-out

permit.status: No permit · sign in at the put-in

items.d: Permits are not required to float the Dolores in Colorado. Boaters sign in at the put-in.
Overnight trips need a fire pan, a portable toilet and a dishwater strainer.
Bradfield campsites are $8 a night. Slickrock parking and launching is $10 a day, paid to the landowner.

A free permit is required year-round for private trips from Gateway, Colorado, to Dewey Bridge, Utah, through Recreation.gov (or by phone to the Moab office at 435-259-7012, 8 a.m. to noon weekdays). The trip leader signs and carries it.
